sections.label: Category E COE quota rules
sections.summary: Category E COEs let the vehicle mix evolve; all categories contribute 10% of their quota, reduced from 25% over three years, with motorcycles in a separate category.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: Category E COEs, which can be used to register vehicles from any category, are intended to allow the vehicle mix to evolve as market demand changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: Currently, all vehicle categories contribute 10% of their quota to Category E.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: This rate has been gradually reduced from 25% over the last three years, with the most recent reduction to 10% taking effect in February 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: Motorcycles are in a separate COE category so that motorcycle buyers need not compete with car buyers for COEs.

sections.label: Category D quota and sub-categories
sections.summary: Category D's quota was about 2,000 last quarter; smaller sub-categories may cause price volatility, and the COE framework will continue to be reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: Last quarter, for instance, the Category D COE quota was about 2,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: Dividing Category D into even smaller sub-categories may result in significant volatility in their COE prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: It was, in fact, for this very reason that the Government Parliamentary Committee that reviewed the COE system back in 1999 had recommended to merge the then-four car categories into the present two.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: We will continue to review the COE framework, including the Category E contribution rate, and make adjustments, if required.
